description: Per-finding coverage manifest. NOT exhaustive — tracks structural gates and high-severity Phase-6/7 closures. Pre-Phase-7 the description claimed to cover 'every shipped audit-finding fix'; R8-FG-21 / R9-P10-009 surfaced the under-claim (manifest covered ~9 of 115+ R6 findings). Phase-7 honest rewrite: (a) every R6/R8 critical fix has an entry, (b) R9 critical fixes have entries, (c) structural gate entries cover archetype classes that subsume many findings collectively (see coverageStrategy: 'structural-gate'), (d) lows / mediums are NOT all listed; the manifest-vs-doc ratio counter at audit-coverage.test.ts:`manifest-vs-audit-doc coverage ratio` reports the gap as informational telemetry. Adding new R10+ findings: critical/high MUST land with manifest entry + locking test (and ideally revertDrill patch); medium/low are operator's call.

findings.summary: executeIntent + executeEncodedCall in contracts.ts skipped safeSubmit, so post-submit errors escaped as plain Error and withIdempotency DELed the claim — contract-call double-spend window on every buy/roll/transferAllPrizes/staking op.

findings.notes: Source-level structural test asserts the safeSubmit import + ≥2 `await safeSubmit(` call sites. Removing either wrapper flips the assertion. Two drills authored: R6-FG-4.patch removes the safeSubmit import (R8-FG-20 import-only revert detector); R6-FG-4-callsite.patch removes one call site keeping the import (R8-FG-20 callsite-only revert detector). Manifest cites the import drill; the callsite drill is on disk for ad-hoc operator use via `npm run audit:revert-drill -- R6-FG-4-callsite` (manifest split would require a new findings-id; the drill file exists for future activation).
